text:
Mikael Granlund is 34, on his sixth NHL team, and about 25 games from 1,000 in the league. In Anaheim he is a 20-minute center with 16 points in 16 games, nine on the power play, and a five-game point streak as the Ducks have won four straight.

The underlying picture is less rosy. The Ducks have scored 8.7 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and at five on five they get only 37.8 percent of the expected goals when he plays, worse than without him. His own finishing is normal (four goals on 3.89 expected), so the luck is in the goals around him, and that is the kind that fades.

This is a player who has always lived on skill rather than size. The Finn went ninth overall in 2010, was Central Scouting's top international skater that year, and Evolving-Hockey had his offense driving play in the 90th percentile among forwards last season. In a young Ducks lineup built around Leo Carlsson, Cutter Gauthier and Beckett Sennecke, he is the veteran passer. Watch his five-on-five minutes; if they shrink, the points will too.
headline: Granlund is nearing 1,000 games on a Ducks power play that won't miss
